reveal.auditorReaction: You estimated a score of 56, but your official Sherpas financial health score is 52—classified as VULNERABLE. You have done a lot right: you own your home, you have built retirement savings, and you prioritize your family. But there is a massive protection vulnerability: Daniel has only $250,000 in life insurance against a recommended minimum of $1,600,000, and Emily has zero coverage! Combined with an $18,000 credit card at a punishing 24.9% APR, your family's safety net has gaping holes.

discoveries.title: THE $1,350,000 PROTECTION CHASM
discoveries.source: Key Metrics — Life Insurance Ratios & Facts
discoveries.explanation: Daniel has $250,000 of coverage against a minimum recommendation of $1.6M. Emily, whose income and household contribution are vital for Oliver (11) and Sophia (9), has $0 in coverage. With a $560,000 mortgage, existing coverage would not even pay off half the house.
discoveries.whyItMatters: If either parent passes, the surviving spouse faces a mortgage and two college tuition bills with inadequate income replacement.
discoveries.auditorRemark: You love your children deeply, but love does not pay off a $560,000 mortgage. A term policy is cheap peace of mind that should have been locked in years ago.

discoveries.title: THE 24.9% CREDIT CARD TRAP
discoveries.explanation: At 24.9% APR, over $370 every single month goes straight into the credit card company’s pockets just for interest charges. It is your single most expensive financial liability.
discoveries.whyItMatters: Paying minimums on a 24.9% card will cost over $15,000 in interest alone over time.
discoveries.auditorRemark: Twenty-four point nine percent is loan shark territory. That card is setting fire to the college money you want to save for Oliver and Sophia.

verdict.doingRight: You have built meaningful equity in your Denver home and have steady dual incomes with a shared commitment to Oliver and Sophia's future.
verdict.needsAttention: Your credit card debt ($18,000 at 24.9%) and lack of umbrella liability coverage expose your family to unnecessary drag and liability risk.
verdict.overlooking: Your catastrophic protection gap: carrying only $250k in term life with two young children and a $560k mortgage means an unexpected tragedy would force a fire sale of the house.
verdict.bottomLine: You have built a great home; now put a roof over it. Lock in proper term life insurance for both of you and declare war on the 24.9% credit card.

mission.title: Secure 20-Year Term Life & Protect The Kids
mission.whyItMatters: Protecting Oliver and Sophia with $1.5M in 20-year term coverage costs roughly $60–$90/month and permanently closes your single most dangerous vulnerability.
mission.firstAction: Request three competitive quotes for 20-year level term life insurance ($1.5M for Daniel, $750k for Emily) before the week ends.
steps: Calculate the required term: 20 years covers Oliver through age 31 and Sophia through age 29.
Obtain term quotes from independent brokerages (Term4Sale or Policygenius) for 20-year level term policies.
Submit the preliminary applications to lock in rates while in good health.
Formulate a plan to attack the 24.9% credit card balance using monthly cash flow once protection is in underwriting.
mission.howToVerify: Both policy applications submitted and confirmation emails received.
